blogs.title: When Neck Swelling Isn’t Ludwig’s Angina: Dermatomyositis in the Differential
blogs.description: A deep dive into how inflammatory myopathies can masquerade as deep neck space infections or idiopathic angioedema. We'll discuss red‑flag clues (non‑painful swelling, lack of fever, subtle skin findings), imaging pitfalls, and a step‑wise diagnostic algorithm for emergency physicians and ENT surgeons to avoid missed dermatomyositis.

blogs.title: Pseudo‑Angioedema in Inflammatory Myopathy: Pathophysiology and Practical Work‑up
blogs.description: Explores the mechanisms behind non‑histamine, non‑bradykinin neck/ facial edema in dermatomyositis and related antibodies (anti‑SAE, anti‑MDA5, anti‑TIF1‑γ). We'll compare true angioedema labs (C1‑INH, complement) with myositis‑related edema, and outline a focused laboratory panel (CK, ANA, myositis antibodies) for rapid bedside triage.

blogs.title: Anti‑SAE1 Dermatomyositis: Clinical Phenotype, Cancer Risk, and Screening Strategies
blogs.description: Reviews the epidemiology of anti‑SAE1 antibodies, their association with cutaneous signs, dysphagia, lung disease, and malignancy. We'll summarize current IMACS cancer‑screening recommendations, risk stratification tools, and propose a pragmatic surveillance plan for clinicians encountering this rare serology.

blogs.title: Aggressive Immunosuppression for Severe Myositis with Airway Involvement: Lessons from a Real‑World Case
blogs.description: Analyzes the therapeutic regimen used—high‑dose IV methylprednisolone, IVIG, mycophenolate, rituximab—and the rationale for avoiding methotrexate in the setting of pulmonary disease. Includes a discussion of dosing schedules, tapering steroids, infection prophylaxis, and monitoring for relapse in patients with life‑threatening muscle edema.

blogs.title: Dysphagia in Dermatomyositis: From Subclinical to Airway Threat
blogs.description: Focuses on the evaluation and management of myositis‑related swallowing dysfunction. We'll cover bedside screening, barium swallow findings, role of early speech‑language pathology, nutritional support (NG tube vs PEG), and how timely immunotherapy can reverse dysphagia.

blogs.title: Imaging the Inflamed Muscles: When FDG‑PET, MRI, and CT Complement Each Other in Myositis
blogs.description: Shows how multimodal imaging clarified the diagnosis in this case—FDG‑PET highlighting diffuse muscle uptake, MRI confirming myositis in deep neck muscles, and CT ruling out infection or neoplasm. We'll provide a practical guide to ordering and interpreting these studies in atypical presentations.
